title: Rheumatic Heart Disease Prevention And Valve-Care Gaps In High-Burden Countries
summary: Build a verified way to measure where people are lost between streptococcal-infection prevention, recurrent-rheumatic-fever prophylaxis, rheumatic-heart-disease diagnosis, referral, and definitive valve care in high-burden settings.
why_it_matters: Ministries of health, national noncommunicable-disease and child-health programme managers, and global-health funders must decide whether scarce resources should first repair benzathine-penicillin supply, primary-care prevention, echocardiographic diagnosis, referral, or valve-care capacity. A replicated cascade map would change that allocation decision while preventing modeled prevalence, medicine procurement, or a single hospital registry from being mistaken for delivered care.

success_metrics.target: Every country or district output separates prevention, prophylaxis, diagnosis, referral, surgery or valve care, and follow-up denominators.
success_metrics.validation_method: A domain reviewer checks each stage for numerator, denominator, event date, setting, missingness, and whether the measure is observed care rather than policy or supply capacity.

success_metrics.target: Every burden, pathway, or implementation claim links to a dated evidence record with method and limitations.
success_metrics.validation_method: Run pnpm validate and spot-check every claim-to-source mapping in evidence.json and evidence.md.

success_metrics.target: At least one independently replicated cascade artifact identifies a measurable bottleneck for programme review without issuing patient-level advice.
success_metrics.validation_method: A replicator reruns the documented analysis and a red-team reviewer confirms that the artifact cannot be read as diagnosis, treatment, or an automatic country ranking.

review_policy.merge_gate: Schema validation, public-health and health-systems domain review, red-team review of clinical and allocation misuse, field-reality review of care pathways, and independent replication for quantitative outputs.
